requirement.description: The Signal class does not implement a __hash__ method, which prevents it from being added to Python sets. This causes TypeError: unhashable type: 'Signal' when trying to collect signals for name assignment in _assign_names_to_signals method.
requirement.contract: The Signal class must implement a __hash__ method that returns a hashable value based on its identity to enable use in sets and dictionaries.
requirement.acceptance: tests/test_hdl_ir.py::ConflictTestCase::test_domain_conflict, tests/test_hdl_ir.py::RhsTestCase::test_slice, tests/test_hdl_ir.py::RhsTestCase::test_operator_unary, and other related tests that currently fail with "TypeError: unhashable type: 'Signal'"

requirement.description: The _assign_names_to_signals method attempts to add Signal objects to a set but fails because Signals are not hashable. This affects signal name assignment and netlist building.
requirement.contract: The method should properly handle Signal objects by ensuring they are hashable or by using alternative data structures that don't require hashing.
requirement.acceptance: tests/test_hdl_ir.py::AssignTestCase::test_simple_trunc, tests/test_hdl_ir.py::AssignTestCase::test_simple_part_short, and other related tests that currently fail with "TypeError: unhashable type: 'Signal'"

requirement.description: There is already a SignalKey class designed to wrap Signal objects for use in dictionaries and sets, but the Signal class itself lacks a __hash__ method.
requirement.contract: The Signal class should implement __hash__ method that aligns with the SignalKey implementation to maintain consistency.
requirement.acceptance: All tests that fail due to unhashable Signal objects should pass after implementing the __hash__ method

requirement.description: SignalDict uses SignalKey to wrap Signals, but Signal itself is not directly hashable, which creates inconsistency in how Signals are used in collections.
requirement.contract: Signal class should implement __hash__ to enable direct use in sets and dictionaries without requiring wrapper classes.
requirement.acceptance: Tests that rely on Signal objects being usable in collections should pass

requirement.description: The DUID base class provides deterministic unique IDs but doesn't provide hashability, which is needed for using Signal objects in sets.
requirement.contract: Add a __hash__ method to Signal that uses its duid to make it hashable while preserving uniqueness.
requirement.acceptance: Signal objects should be usable in sets and dictionaries without throwing TypeError
